meta.note: Canonical brand values. Read these verbatim; never approximate brand colors or type from memory. Contains brand expression only — no commercial or strategic information.
meta.sourceOfTruth: The production marketing site (site/public/assets/css/theme.min.css + bootstrap.min.css 5.0.2). Values were EXTRACTED from shipped CSS, not designed here. Full extraction record: INVENTORY.md.
meta.v3Change: v2.x drifted from the shipped site — it specified cardRadius 14px (real: 8px), contentWidth 1080px (real: 1140px), pillRadius 999px (real: 25px), body 16px/1.7 (real: 15px), and a 2-stop soft gradient (real: 3-stop, warm). Pages built from v2.x tokens therefore drifted by construction; that is what happened to the AI Practice page. v3.0 reconciles every DESCRIPTIVE token to production.

twoKindsOfToken.descriptive: What the brand IS — color, gradient, type, spacing, layout, skew. Production is the source of truth. Marked "status": "production". If these disagree with the shipped site, the token is wrong, not the site.
twoKindsOfToken.prescriptive: What the brand SHOULD DO — accessibility, motion, dataViz, voice, slide decks. These are POLICY and production does not yet satisfy all of them. Marked "status": "proposed" where the shipped site conflicts. Never assume a "proposed" value is what the site currently does.

meta.readingGuide: Building something new that must match the existing site → use "production" values only. Improving the system deliberately → "proposed" values are the agreed target, but changing them is a decision, not a default.

_tiers.note: Colors are organized in three tiers. Do not promote a color between tiers without a brand decision.
_tiers.surface: The soft ground is a GRADIENT, not a set of colors. mint / ice / sand exist ONLY as stops within `gradient.soft` — never fill a surface with one of them alone, and never list them as standalone brand colors.

navy.use: The brand's ground state — hero and section backgrounds, card bodies, body text, logo plane body on light grounds. The LIGHTER of the two navies.

navyDeep.v3Correction: Was #081F37 in v2.x — the shipped footer is #05203a. Corrected to match.

green.use: THE brand green. Buttons, eyebrows, fills, icons, highlights, accents on any ground; large surfaces.
green.knownTypo: #54b886 appears in some shipped rules (buttons, explore links) — a one-digit typo of this value. Never propagate it; always use #54B987.

textOnLightGrounds.guidance: Green measures 2.4:1 on white and fails WCAG AA as text — greenInk is the accessible substitute. Production DOES use raw green for eyebrows on light grounds, so this is an open gap, not current behavior.

textOnGreenFill.guidance: RESOLVED: the primary button is a GREEN FILL WITH WHITE TEXT, matching production. New work uses white — this is no longer an open question.
textOnGreenFill.accessibilityFootnote: White-on-green measures ~2.4:1, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for normal text; it clears the 3:1 large-text threshold, so at the shipped 16px Bold it is borderline. If a future audit requires AA here, the lever is DARKENING THE GREEN behind white text — not reverting the text to navy, which would undo the decision.

greenPunch.use: Punch accent ONLY. At most one intentional emphasis moment per page or asset. Never for buttons, labels, charts, or recurring UI.

greenInk.use: ACCESSIBLE TEXT VARIANT of green — eyebrows, links, inline emphasis on light grounds. 6.2:1 on white, passes WCAG AA. Same hue family as green.

teal.use: Heritage accent. Fills, dark-ground text, data viz series 3. NOT for text on light grounds (2.8:1, fails WCAG AA) — use tealInk.

tealInk.use: ACCESSIBLE TEXT VARIANT of teal — subheads, links, mid-sentence callouts on light grounds. 5.7:1 on white, passes WCAG AA.

steel.use: Secondary blue. Data viz series 2, supporting UI, diagrams. Passes AA as text on white (6.2:1) already.

slate.use: Muted blue-gray. Borders, gridlines, decorative use, text on DARK grounds only. NOT for text on light grounds (2.6:1, fails WCAG AA) — use inkMuted.

inkMuted.use: ACCESSIBLE TEXT VARIANT of slate — captions, secondary labels, chart axis text on light grounds. 5.1:1 on white, passes WCAG AA.

gray.use: DECK SYSTEM ONLY — slide headers and body text on white. Deliberately absent from the marketing-site palette; see the Decks tab. Never use this on the website.

no.use: "Don't"/error fill and borders — decorative use only. NOT for text (3.4:1, fails WCAG AA) — use noInk.

noInk.use: ACCESSIBLE TEXT VARIANT of no — "don't" tags, form error text/messages on light grounds. 6.6:1 on white, passes WCAG AA.

coral.use: ILLUSTRATION ONLY. The glowing path/node accent in paper-cut scenes. Never a UI, chart, or text color.

mint.use: Soft gradient stop A (0%). Light card and panel surfaces.
mint.v3Correction: Was #EEF8EC in v2.x. The shipped gradient starts at #e8fefb — a cooler, lighter aqua. Corrected.

ice.use: Soft gradient stop B (55%). The midpoint of the soft ground.

sand.use: Soft gradient stop C (100%). The WARM stop that gives This Waay grounds their signature cool-to-warm shift.
sand.v3Addition: Missing entirely from v2.x, which modelled the soft ground as a 2-stop cool gradient. The warmth at the far corner is what makes the real cards feel like paper rather than glass — reproducing the ground without it is the most visible single cause of 'close but not right'.

mutedOnLight.use: Body/secondary copy on light and soft grounds — the site's workhorse muted text. Navy at 65%, not a separate grey.
mutedOnLight.v3Addition: Production expresses muted text as navy-with-opacity, never as a distinct grey token. New work must do the same or the copy reads subtly off-hue.

white.use: A PRIMARY GROUND, not an absence. The page alternates navy and white sections — white carries half the page rhythm. Also the logo plane body on navy grounds.
white.v3Change: Promoted to primary. Previously listed as an afterthought, which understated that white is one of the two grounds the whole section rhythm is built from.

soft.use: THE canonical light surface — segment cards, service cards, testimonial and pricing panels, alternating sections. Cool aqua into warm sand.
soft.v3Correction: Was a 2-stop cool gradient (#EEF8EC → #F2FBFB) in v2.x. The shipped value is 3 stops and ends WARM. This single token accounts for most of the 'the cards look almost right' gap.

softWarm.use: The 4-stop variant used behind the why-us float-panel cards. Warm at BOTH ends, cool through the middle — a softer, more neutral ground than `soft`.

softVariants.note: Production contains ~5 near-identical soft-gradient recipes (the testimonial panel puts its midpoint at 66% rather than 55%, etc.). `soft` and `softWarm` are the two proposed canonical survivors; the rest should collapse into them. Until that consolidation ships, match the specific section you are extending rather than assuming `soft`.

green.use: Counts as a punch usage — same one-per-asset rule.

wing.use: Official paper-plane wing: deep teal at tail to light green at nose. Motif use only.

onDarkSurface.note: Translucent-white surface for cards that sit on a navy ground (e.g. the track/plan card). Needs the navy backdrop to read — not self-contained like the light-ground card patterns above.

cardBorder.use: Card border and internal dividers on navy grounds.

textBody.use: Body copy and list items on navy. ~9:1, passes WCAG AA.

textMeta.use: De-emphasized meta text on navy (timing, tags). Floor is 60% — 45% measures ~4.1:1 on navy and fails AA; 60% clears 4.5:1.

fallback.use: Approved free substitute when Axiforma is unavailable. The ONLY acceptable substitute.

model.note: PRODUCTION DOES NOT USE FONT-WEIGHT. Each cut is a separately-named self-hosted family declared at font-weight:normal, and hierarchy is selected by family NAME. v2.x modelled this as one family + numeric weights (400/500/600/700), which is not what ships and silently renders the wrong cut when a build sets font-weight:700 against a family that has no bold.

AxiformaRegular.use: Body copy, hero body, captions, footer links.

AxiformaMedium.use: Card body copy, form labels, muted secondary text.

AxiformaSemiBold.use: Hero H1 — the one place SemiBold leads.

AxiformaExtraBold.use: H2 section headings and every card title (h5). THE dominant heading cut across the site.
AxiformaExtraBold.v3Addition: Absent from v2.x entirely, despite carrying nearly all heading weight in production.

model.stack: 'AxiformaExtraBold','Poppins','Segoe UI',sans-serif — build the stack per named family, not per weight.

weightEquivalents.note: The weightEquivalent numbers above exist ONLY to map into environments that require numeric weights (Figma variable modes, PPTX export, CSS variable fonts). They are a translation layer, never a substitute for selecting the named family in web work.

scale.note: PRODUCTION USES FIXED PIXEL SIZES, not fluid clamps. v2.x specified clamp() ranges that never matched the site at any viewport. Sizes below are the shipped values.

heroH1.note: The homepage hero headline — the one place green leads at display size and the one place SemiBold outranks ExtraBold. Other heroes vary: assessment ships a white H1.

h2.note: Section headings. Navy on light grounds, white on navy.

h5.note: EVERY card title. The most-used heading in the system. Why-us float cards drop to 18px.

body.note: v2.x said 16px/1.7. The site ships 15px with line-height:normal (~1.2).

cardBody.note: Card and segment copy — Medium at 65% navy, not Regular. Approach cards ship 16px.

eyebrow.note: Tracking is an absolute 2.76px at 12px (≈0.23em). Assessment and AI Practice ship 1.5px/1.6px — an unresolved inconsistency; 2.76px is the theme default and the proposed canonical.

bodyLeading.note: Production's line-height:normal (~1.2) is tight for sustained reading. 1.6 is the proposed improvement for NEW long-form work — it will not match existing pages, so do not retrofit shipped pages without a decision.

sizeScale.note: Every font-size in the system (index.html) resolves to one of these 10 fixed steps, plus the dedicated h1/h2/body/lede sizes above. Consolidated from ~36 unrelated one-off values that had accumulated with no shared scale — every element now references one step, so a future size change happens in one place.

2xs.use: Finest print — nav tagline, deck micro-eyebrow, tiny badges

xs.use: Fine meta text — slide numbers, breadcrumb, footer links

sm.use: Small labels — eyebrows, category-ish small text

md.use: The dominant secondary/caption size across cards and captions

lg.use: Near-body UI text — buttons, form fields, list copy

xl.use: Card titles, sub-headings (equal to the lede size)

5xl.use: The largest decorative glyph (testimonial quote mark)

chassis.note: THE SITE'S RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOUR IS BOOTSTRAP, NOT BESPOKE. Do not re-author the grid. Layout = Bootstrap `container` / `row` / `col-lg-*`; This Waay components live INSIDE those columns and never set their own widths, breakpoints, or gutters. Re-implementing the grid with hand-rolled CSS grid is the single fastest way to lose the site's whitespace and component sizing — it is what made the first rebuild attempt read as 'too far off'.
chassis.cardRow: Three-up card sections are `.row` + three `.col-lg-4` — they collapse to full width below 992px, not at a custom breakpoint.
chassis.v3Correction: v2.x specified contentWidth 1080px and a bespoke `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(255px,1fr))` card grid. Neither exists in production.

textMeasure.note: Not enforced in production, where measure is whatever the Bootstrap column yields. Good practice for new long-form work.

cardRadius.note: Every `.box` on the site. v2.x said 14px — that value is real but belongs ONLY to the on-navy track card.

exceptions.aiPractice: 16px / 20px — drift introduced by the AI Practice page; should collapse to 8px

pillRadius.note: Buttons. v2.x said 999px — a fully-round pill. At the shipped 50px button height 25px IS effectively round, but the literal value matters for smaller buttons and for Figma, where 999px produces a different corner on any non-50px height.

inputRadius.note: Form fields are nearly square — a deliberate contrast against the round buttons.

cardGap.note: Bootstrap default gutter (var(--bs-gutter-x), 1.5rem) — inherited, not set by components.

sectionPad.note: There is NO single section-padding token in production; each section ships its own. Documented per-section in INVENTORY. v2.x's clamp(56px,8vw,110px) is not used anywhere.

pageRhythm.note: THERE IS NO FIXED PAGE TEMPLATE, and the page does NOT alternate. v2.x described 'navy hero, then ALTERNATING navy / soft-gradient sections' — production does not do this. Pages open on navy and close on navy; between them the ground changes between navy and a light ground (white or soft gradient) driven by CONTENT, not a repeating pattern.
pageRhythm.rule: Sections that belong together share a ground and run consecutively. The ground changes when the subject changes. Consecutive same-ground sections are correct and common — not a mistake to be 'fixed' by alternating.
pageRhythm.evidence: The actual homepage in DOM order: navy (hero) → white (logo cloud) → white (why-us) → navy (who-we-serve) → navy (services) → white (work) → white (about) → white (testimonials) → white (approach) → navy+maze (contact) → navyDeep (footer). Navy runs twice consecutively; white runs FOUR times.
pageRhythm.invariants: What IS consistent: pages open and close on navy; every section uses the centered eyebrow → H2 → lede lockup; every ground CHANGE is carried by an angled break.
pageRhythm.angledBreaks: The angle marks a change, so it appears ONLY where the ground actually changes. Consecutive same-ground sections run together with no break. See the `skew` block — -2deg is the section default.

systemRules.note: Page-agnostic rules adopted 2026-08 after building the AI Practice page on the system. Each one exists because its absence produced a visible defect.

measure.rule: Every block of running text is capped. Long lines are the most common readability failure on wide screens.
measure.why: Headings get a much shorter measure than body copy on purpose — it forces them to break on meaning rather than at the container edge, which is what prevents stranded words in display type.

rag.balance: text-wrap:balance on headings, card titles, and ledes — evens line lengths on SHORT text in WIDE containers.
rag.pretty: text-wrap:pretty on paragraphs, list items, and long quotes — fixes the last-line widow on LONG text.
rag.hyphens: none on all headings — display type never hyphenates.
rag.pitfall: balance is WRONG in a narrow column: in a col-lg-3 card it shortens every line and the rag goes stubby. Balance short text in wide containers; pretty long text in narrow ones.

angledBreak.rule: The diagonal must sit FLUSH against the grounds above and below (no sliver of a third colour) and must run EDGE TO EDGE of the viewport.
angledBreak.how: A skewed element rotates about its own centre, so its far corners lift out of its box. The skewed ground is a ::before that OVERSHOOTS its section — horizontally (left/right: -8vw) so the diagonal always reaches both viewport edges, and vertically (~2.2vw) so consecutive sections overlap rather than leaving a gap.
angledBreak.clearanceRule: The diagonal rises above the section's own box by roughly (width / 2) * tan(2deg) ~ 26px at desktop, PLUS the overshoot. A section on either side of a break needs >= 90px of vertical padding, or its last line of copy slides under the neighbouring ground. This is the most common defect when the motif is rebuilt.

ghostHover.rule: On hover/focus a ghost button's fill becomes its OUTLINE colour, and the label knocks out to the ground it was sitting on. Never a third colour, never a tint.
ghostHover.onLight: green outline -> green fill, white label
ghostHover.onNavy: white outline -> white fill, navy label

groundOwnership.rule: A component that carries its own ground owns its own text colour AND its own controls — not just text. A light card dropped into a navy section must not inherit that section's light-on-dark styling.
groundOwnership.failureMode: White text on a soft-gradient card reads as blank. An on-navy ghost button (white outline) rendered inside a light card that itself sits inside a navy section is the SAME bug one level down — a section-scoped rule like `.tw-on-navy .tw-btn--ghost` only knows the section's ground, not the actual ground the button is sitting on.
groundOwnership.how: Any component with its own ground — including buttons and list markers inside it — sets those colours at a specificity high enough to beat a section-level descendant selector (e.g. doubled class), without reaching for !important. A bare class selector LOSES to a descendant selector like `.tw-step p` — that collision silently muted a green subtitle during the AI Practice build.
groundOwnership.preferExtendOverInvent: A from-scratch card is a new opportunity to reintroduce this exact bug. Prefer extending an already-portable component (e.g. the generic content card) over inventing a new one — a CTA block built as its own translucent-on-dark card broke the moment its section's ground changed; replacing it with the portable content card removed the bug rather than patched it.
groundOwnership.specificityCheck: If the base selector for an element you're overriding already uses a doubled class, a single-class colour modifier will lose SILENTLY. Match or exceed the doubled pattern, or the override never applies and the failure is invisible until computed style is inspected.

straddleElement.rule: A card or banner that visually bridges the boundary between two sections rather than living inside one.
straddleElement.how: Built as the FIRST element of the section that comes AFTER the boundary. Correct mechanism is `transform:translateY(-overlap)` + `margin-bottom:-overlap` on the SAME element (`.tw-overlap`), NOT `margin-top`. The break renders behind it (z-index), so the diagonal appears to pass under the straddling element.
straddleElement.notMarginTop: REWRITTEN 2026-08 after this shipped broken twice. A negative margin-top on the first child of a zero-padding, zero-border parent COLLAPSES THROUGH the parent — it drags the SECTION's own box (and the diagonal painted by that section) up with it, rather than moving the child within a fixed section. Result: changing the overlap amount moves the card AND the boundary together as a rigid unit, so the card's position relative to the boundary barely changes no matter what value is chosen — a card that looks correctly tuned by the numbers but sits almost entirely on one side of the seam when rendered. `transform` repaints pixels without touching layout, so the section (and the boundary it paints) stay exactly where normal flow puts them; the paired `margin-bottom` (between two siblings, not into the parent) gives back the flow space the lift no longer needs.
straddleElement.blockFormattingContext: Give `.tw-overlap` itself `display:flow-root`. Without it, a NESTED negative margin one level down re-introduces the exact same collapse — Bootstrap's own row gutter (`.g-4` sets `.row{margin-top:-gutter}`) is exactly that pattern, and silently ate part of the lift.
straddleElement.noRedundantPadding: The section holding the straddle needs ZERO top padding (use a variant like `.pad-after-overlap`, not the generic `.pad`) — the straddling element supplies its own clearance via the overlap value. Generic top padding on the section adds an UNTUNED offset on top of the overlap math and desyncs the numbers from what actually renders.
straddleElement.verifyAgainstRealPixels: Verify the split with actual rendered pixels (screenshot + sample colour on both sides of the line at an x with no other content), not box-model arithmetic alone — comparing two DOM measurements that both depend on the same collapsing margin can validate a bug against itself and report success. The diagonal ALSO renders above the raw section-boundary Y by the deliberate overshoot amount (~2.2vw, RULE 3) plus a skew-dependent slope across the row's width (~44px total at -2deg over 1280px) — account for both when computing the overlap value a naive box-model read will not.
straddleElement.clearanceForTallElements: A tall straddling element (e.g. a banner far taller than an entry card) needs correspondingly more lift to bisect the line — which can eat into the CONTENT above it, not just the section's padding. Increase that content's own bottom clearance to match, or the straddle will visually collide with whatever precedes it.
examples: Two entry cards spanning a hero into the section below it
An offer banner spanning the boundary between two body sections
straddleElement.note: Same mechanism regardless of which two grounds are involved — no per-case CSS needed.
straddleElement.clearance: Give the copy above it room to breathe FIRST — production runs a generous gap between the preceding copy (e.g. a hero's subhead) and the top of the straddling element, well beyond the ~90px minimum the angled-break clearance rule requires. Tune the straddle for an even split (roughly half the element above the boundary, half below) as a separate step from that breathing room.

textCtaWithArrow.rule: A link styled as text, not a button, ending in a trailing arrow that nudges forward on hover/focus. Extends production's `.link-txt` pattern ("Click to learn more").
textCtaWithArrow.use: Where a call to action shouldn't compete with the page's real buttons — e.g. closing out one of several parallel content blocks.

heroMeasureException.rule: Hero-scale H1s (46px+) do NOT take the standard measure.headDisplay token (22ch) — that value is tuned for in-page H2s at 40px. Applying it to a larger hero headline collapses it to one line too many.
heroMeasureException.how: Let the hero H1 size to its actual column width (with rag balance still applied) and verify the RENDERED line count for that specific headline rather than assuming a token value transfers.

skew.note: The signature motif — shallow diagonal breaks echoing the plane wing. Applied as `transform: skew(0deg, Ndeg)` on a `::before` pseudo-element behind the content, never on the content itself (which would shear the type). v2.x described this loosely as '2-4 degrees'; these are the exact shipped angles.

section.use: Section breaks and the hero band. The default.

card.use: Card panels — the float-panel motif. Steepest and most characteristic.

components.note: The component taxonomy extracted from production. Each entry is one component; each `variantAxes` entry is one axis of variation. Structured this way so it maps 1:1 onto Figma component properties (axis → property, values → property options) and onto CSS modifier classes. Full anatomy, per-section values, and provenance live in INVENTORY.md §10-12.
components.layoutRule: NO component defines its own width, breakpoint, or outer margin. Width comes from the Bootstrap column it sits in. This is what makes a component reusable across pages.

style: white (white fill, green text — for navy grounds)

button.note: Only `lg` ships today; md/sm are proposed additions. Hover inverts fill and text rather than darkening.

floatPanelCard.anatomy: A transparent box whose `::before` is a skewed colored panel starting PARTWAY DOWN (60-90px), with a large figure floating above and overlapping the panel's top edge. This overlap is the brand's most recognizable card gesture.

segmentCard.anatomy: Solid soft-gradient card, 8px radius, with a figure pulled UP 40px so it breaks the card's top edge. Title sits 55px below to clear the figure.
segmentCard.correction2026_08: Previously documented as a uniform 'circular badge' — wrong. The figure is NOT a fixed shape; it's whatever pre-rendered icon graphic ships for that segment, and the three real assets disagree with each other.

realAssets.shape: navy circle, green 3px ring, white clipboard+check icon, green accent circle
navy circle, green 3px ring, white document+lines icon, green sparkle accent
green (#72B68A, a distinct shade from --tw-green) skewed rectangle, white branching-path icon — same skew motif as the float-panel card, at icon scale

segmentCard.note: Used for the three homepage audience segments ("Who We Serve"). Real asset files: site/public/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/{icon06,icon07,icon09}.svg.

cardGrounds.note: The ground axis every card type can take.

cardTypes.note: 13 distinct card types are catalogued in INVENTORY §10. The consolidation target is that all of them are (cardType × ground × badgePlacement) rather than 13 unrelated patterns.
cardTypes.flipCardCorrection: Title and description live INSIDE the card, never below it: front = image + bottom gradient scrim carrying the title; back (hover/focus) = full title + short description + CTA, centered on the accent-colour mask. Corrected 2026-08 after a rebuild rendered them as page copy underneath the card — the style guide's own specimen never caught this because its demo cell didn't carry real, full-length copy. Test components with real content, not placeholder labels.

type: proprietary shield (metallic rim, star-field navy face, white icon)
icon tile (rounded square / circle / punch gradient)
placement: floating above (overlaps panel top — the signature)

badge.removed2026_08: "flat vector" (navy circle, green ring, white icon) was removed from this axis — it wasn't a deliberate, reusable type. It generalized two of the homepage segment icons (segmentCard below) that happen to share a look into a badge "type" that was never actually a template. See segmentCard for what those assets really are.
badge.shieldNote: The shield's metallic chrome ships as RASTER (image26-31.webp), not vector. An SVG recreation (silver-rim frame + navy star-field face, white icon slot) now exists — see shieldRoster below — and is required for the Figma library.

shieldRoster.note: 8 shield+icon pairings now in use across service/capability labeling. Same #shield frame every time; only the inner icon (white, ~40% of shield width, centered ~43% down) changes.

badge.iconSource: Heroicons — the shipped dimension icons are literally sparkles / squares-2x2 / user-plus / arrow-trending-up. Icons are referenced BY NAME on a 24px grid, ~1.7 stroke, with at most one green accent.
badge.iconSourceForward: Google Material Icons (https://github.com/google/material-design-icons) — decided 2026-08 as the source for any NEW iconography introduced going forward. Sits alongside, not in place of, Heroicons (existing single-tone icons) and the studio's own pre-rendered graphic assets (shield chrome, segmentCard figures) — those stay as they are.

list.numberedStepLayout: Numbered step works stacked (default) OR as a horizontal row of columns — same markup, wrapped in the Bootstrap grid instead of a single column. No separate horizontal component needed. The numeral's placement changes with the layout: floated left of the text works in one wide column, but leaves a visibly orphaned gap in a narrower row column with no shared alignment. In the row layout, stack the numeral directly above the title instead (same counter, no longer absolutely positioned).

iconSourceForward.rule: Any NEW iconography introduced into the system going forward should be pulled from this library rather than hand-drawn.
iconSourceForward.supersedes: A duotone-treatment experiment (Material Symbols glyphs + a custom two-layer navy/green halo effect) was built 2026-08, did not meet the mark on review, and was discarded — its CSS, sprite file, and preview page were removed. See badge.removed2026_08 for the related 'flat vector' badge-type removal (same cleanup pass, different cause).
iconSourceForward.doesNotReplace: Heroicons (existing single-tone icons already in production) and the studio's own pre-rendered graphic assets (shield chrome, segmentCard figures) — those stay as they are.

flightPath.note: Hand-flown dotted trail (round caps, stroke-dasharray 0.1 8) containing at least one loop. BRIDGES EXACTLY TWO SECTIONS at a transition — used 1-2x per page, never on every section. Real assets: line-hero, line-whowe, line-testimonials, line-foot, dots.svg.

navigation.structure: Two-row layout: logo/wordmark on its own first row, a second row of section-group buttons below it. Each group button (aria-expanded + aria-controls) discloses a subsection dropdown of links — click/keyboard-triggered only, never hover-only. Only one group open at a time; Escape and outside-click/focus-out close it.

dataViz.labels: Axiforma/Poppins, slate for axes, navy for emphasis, 8-11px
dataViz.strokeWeight: 3px with 3px radius on bars and line caps
dataViz.rules: No 3D, no heavy borders, no chart-junk, no background fills. Punch green never appears in charts.

motif.paperPlane: Wing is the gradient blade (#62D38C nose to #30737B tail). Body navy on light grounds, white on navy. Never outlined, never flat green. Use the official SVG paths, not redrawn geometry.
motif.flightPath: Round dots (stroke-dasharray 0.1 8, round caps, ~3px), navy on light / white on navy. Every trail includes at least one loop. Never straight, never dashed. Five canonical variants — A Single loop, B S-wave, C Tight coil, D Wide arc, E Double curl — are defined in the style guide. New paths should follow the same hand-flown character.
motif.icons: Bold navy outlines (~3.5px at 48px grid) with a single flat green fill element. On navy, outlines invert to white; green fills stay green.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 AA — the baseline for every This Waay and client deliverable, not a follow-up pass.
accessibility.textOnLight: Use greenInk / tealInk / inkMuted / noInk for text on white or soft-gradient grounds. The raw saturated hues (green, teal, slate, no) are fills/large-surfaces/dark-ground text only.
accessibility.textOnGreenOrTealFill: Navy text, never white. White-on-green and white-on-teal measure ~2.4-2.8:1 and fail AA; navy-on-green/teal measures 5.2-6:1 and passes.

focusRing.colorOnDark: greenPunch (green-bright) — greenInk does not have enough contrast on navy grounds

accessibility.structure: One <main> landmark, one <h1>, sequential <h2>s, a skip-to-content link as the first focusable element.
accessibility.keyboardAndWidgets: Every clickable element is a real button/link, or has role + tabindex="0" + a keydown handler. Async state changes announce via aria-live="polite", not a visual-only change. Prefer native elements (button, details/summary, dialog) over custom-built equivalents — they carry keyboard support and semantics for free.
accessibility.imagesAndIcons: Decorative SVGs/icons get aria-hidden="true". Meaningful ones (logo, narrative illustration used as a hero) get role="img" + a real aria-label/alt describing the meaning, not the literal scene.
accessibility.forms: Every field has a visible, programmatically associated <label>. Required fields are marked with text, not an asterisk-only color cue. Errors use aria-describedby + role="alert", not color alone.
accessibility.dataViz: Never distinguish series by color alone — pair color with a line style, marker shape, or a direct label (WCAG 1.4.1).

motion.principle: Purposeful and directional, echoing the flight-path metaphor. Never decorative-for-its-own-sake.

easing.note: No bounce, spring-overshoot, or elastic easing.

motion.signatureMotion: Flight-path draw-on: one-time stroke-dashoffset reveal, ~2.4s ease-out, for hero/section entrances. Never looping.
mustNeverAnimate: autoplaying/looping motion with no pause control (WCAG 2.2.2)
anything flashing more than 3 times per second (WCAG 2.3.1)
motion as the only carrier of meaning
motion.reducedMotionContract: Every new animated component defines its own prefers-reduced-motion fallback next to the animation itself — not reliant on a single global reset alone.
motion.slideDecks: Fade or cut transitions only, no per-slide novelty transitions, always presenter-controlled — never auto-advance.

slideDeck.isSeparateSurface: Decks are a DISTINCT surface from the marketing site, documented on their own tab in the style guide. Do not apply site tokens to decks or deck tokens to the site. Key differences: grounds are white or navy ONLY (no soft gradients — they wash out projected); Deck Gray #595959 is deck-only and deliberately absent from the site palette; text minimum is ~18px @1080p (larger than web); motion is fade/cut only; the canvas is a fixed 16:9, not a responsive breakpoint system.

deckGray.use: Slide headers and body text on white. NEVER used on the marketing site.

slideDeck.numbering: bottom-right; omitted on title and closing slides
slideDeck.presenterNotes: below the slide, never on it
slideDeck.minTextSize: ~18px equivalent at 1080p — larger than web body minimums for projected/shared-screen legibility
slideDeck.contrastAndMotion: Same rules as web — see accessibility and motion blocks.
